title: Remplacement du ponceau au 123 rue du Vieux Chemin
Denmark – Construction work – Totalentrepriseudbud Afdeling 65 Sættekilde
description: Opgaven omfatter opførelse af 56 nye almene boliger samt et fælleshus og udendørsarealer i totalentreprise indenfor den økonomiske ramme. 56 boliger samt fælleshus skal opføres på matrikel nr. 17bb og 17 bc Bellinge By, Bellinge med et areal på 4.987 m². Med projektet ønsker Civica at skabe rammerne for et levende og fremtidssikret boligmiljø, hvor grøn omstilling og fællesskab er en naturlig del af hverdagen. Bebyggelsen forventes at kunne tiltrække en alsidig beboersammensætning, ved at tilbyde forskellige måder at bo på, et kvalitetsrigt og trygt nærmiljø, indbydende uderum og arkitektonisk kvalitet. Bellinge Fælled er allerede et attraktivt boligområde i den sydvestlige del af Odense med god adgang til skole, daginstitutioner, grønne områder og kollektiv trafik. Området er præget af et familievenligt miljø og et stærkt lokalt fællesskab. En ny almen familieboligafdeling vil kunne bidrage positivt til lokalmiljøet, ved at understøtte et differentieret boligudbud, der kan tiltrække en bred variation af borgere.

title: Finland – Programming services of packaged software products – e-Forms 2023 / EU / HUS 486-2023 Apteekin toiminnanohjausjärjestelmä ohjelmistopalveluna
description: HUS pyytää tarjoustanne ohjelmistopalvelusta, jolla hoidetaan HUS Apteekin toiminnanohjausta kattaen liitteissä kuvatut toiminnan osa-alueet. Hankittavaan ohjelmistopalveluun konfiguroidaan HUS Apteekin lääkkeiden hallinnointia koskevia prosesseja ja tietoja. Ohjelmistopalvelun tulee integroitua HUSin muussa toiminnanohjauksessaan käyttämiin järjestelmiin (esim. Oracle Fusion Cloud). Tarjouspyynnön liitteissä (liite 0 ja liitteet 1: Nykytoiminnan kuvaus) on kuvattu nykytoiminnan laajuutta sanallisin kuvauksin eri toiminta-alueittain. Kuvauksien tarkoitus on perehdyttää tarjoajaa HUS Apteekin nykytoimintaan. Liitteissä (liitteet 2: Tavoitetilan kuvaus) on kuvattu hankinnan kohteelle asetettuja vaatimuksia toiminta-aluekohtaisesti erilaisin prosessikuvauksin ja listatuilla vaatimuksilla. Tämän tarkoituksena on ilmaista tarjoajille toiminnanohjaukselle asetettavia vähimmäisvaatimuksia. Lisäksi on kuvattu tavoitteita nykytoiminnan kehittämiseksi. Tarkoituksenamme on korvata nykyjärjestelmä ohjelmistopalvelulla (SaaS), joka mahdollistaa prosessien kehittämisen ja turvaa laadullisesti vakaan toiminnan. HUS hakee SaaS-pohjaista ohjelmistopalvelua, jonka tulee pohjautua tuotantokäytössä jo olevaan ja valmiiseen ohjelmistoon ja tilaajalle siitä konfiguroitavaan ratkaisuun. Hanke on suunniteltu aikataulultaan sellaiseksi, että ohjelmistopalvelu otetaan käyttöön vuoden 2028 aikana. Hanke käynnistetään määrittelyvaiheella, jossa tarkennetaan tehdyt kuvaukset voittaneen tarjoajan tarjoamaa ohjelmistopalvelua vasten ja näin varmistetaan, että kyseinen ohjelmistopalvelu täyttää asetetut vaatimukset ja tarjoaa selkeän kehityspolun. Tässä määrittelyvaiheessa myös tarkennetaan käyttöönottoprojektin suunnitelma sellaiselle tasolle, että osapuolet voivat sitoutua projektin toteutukseen. Määrittelyvaihe on aikaperusteisesti laskutettava, maksimissaan 50 000 euroa ja kestoltaan enintään neljä kuukautta. Liitteessä Käyttöönottoprojektin kuvaus on tarkemmin selostettu mitä määrittelyvaiheessa tulee tuottaa. Määrittelyvaiheen jälkeen molemmilla osapuolilla on, niin halutessaan, mahdollisuus luopua hankkeesta. Määrittelyvaiheen jälkeen tilaaja ja tarjoaja neuvottelevat tarjouspyynnössä esitetyllä tavoin hankkeelle tavoitetyömäärän ja -hinnan. Muissa tarjouspyynnön liitteissä on kuvattu käyttöönottoprojektiin, jatkuviin palveluihin ja tietoturvaan liittyviä vaatimuksia. Ohjelmistopalvelun tulee olla tavanomaisella tavalla integroitavissa erilaisiin hallinnollisiin järjestelmiin. Ohjelmistopalvelun liittymiä on esitetty liitteessä "Integraatiot". Oracle FINA -liittymät on yksittäisenä kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 2.9.3. Liite "Sopimusluonnos" kattaa sekä käyttöönottovaiheen että jatkuvien palveluiden aikaisen toiminnan. Liitteessä "Hintalomake" on kuvattu tarjousten Vertailuhinnan laskenta ja menettelyt Tavoitehinnan muodostamiseksi.

title: Finland – Construction materials – Rakennustarvikkeet / Loviisa
description: Numera Palvelut Oy pyytää tarjouksia rakennustarvikkeista tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaan. Hankinta sisältää puutavaran, rakennustarvikkeet, maalaus-, laatoitus-, betoninkorjaus- ja tasoitustuotteet Loviisan alueella. Hankinta sisältää erilaiset rakentamisessa tarvittavat tarvikkeet kuten levyt, harkot, verkot, eristeet, laastit, massat, tasoitteet, maalit, maalaustarvikkeet, laatat, lattianpäällysteet, ovet ja karmit. Lisäksi hankinta sisältää laudat, paneelit, saha- ja höylätavaran, kesto- ja kertopuun sekä listat. Hankinta sisältää myös sekalaiset rautakauppatuotteet kuten sähkö- ja akkukäyttöiset käsityökalut, vetimet, naulakot, hyllyt, telineet ja piha-, kiinteistö- ja puutarhatarvikkeet. Hankinta ei sisällä käsityökaluja, kiinnitystarvikkeita, pienkemikaaleja, henkilönsuojaimia, suoja-asusteita eikä kiinteistöjen LVI- tai sähkötarvikkeita. Kilpailutus suoritetaan nopeutetulla avoimella menettelyllä, jonka perusteella valitaan yksi (1) eniten pisteitä saanut sopimustoimittaja. Kilpailutuksen valintaperusteena on kokonaistaloudellinen edullisuus hinnan painoarvon ollessa 100 pistettä. Tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa laadulle asetetut vähimmäisvaatimukset mahdollistavat vertailun ainoastaan hinnalla. Sopimuskausi on määräaikainen neljä (4) vuotta. Sopimuskausi alkaa aikaisintaan hankintapäätöksen saatua lainvoiman tai markkinaoikeuden annettua sopimukselle täytäntöönpanoluvan. Sopimuksen irtisanomisaika on molempien sopijapuolten ja hankintaan sitoutuneiden Numera Palvelut Oy:n asiakasyhteisöjen osalta kuusi (6) kuukautta määräaikaisuudesta huolimatta. Tavoitteena on, että sopimuskausi alkaa syyskuussa 2026 (arvio). Osatarjouksia osakokonaisuuden sisällä ei hyväksytä. Rinnakkaisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä. Tarjoaja sitoutuu tarjouksellaan kaikkiin tarjouspyynnössä esitettyihin ehtoihin. Hankintayksiköllä on oikeus tarkistaa tarjoajan tarjousasiakirjoissa antamat tiedot ennen hankintapäätöksen tekemistä. Mikäli annetut tiedot eivät pidä paikkansa, tarjous hylätään. HUOM! Tarjouspalvelun käyttöön liittyvissä ongelmissa tarjoajan tulee olla yhteydessä Cloudia-tukeen yhteydenottolomakkeella tai numeroon 020 766 1075. Numera Palvelut Oy ei vastaa Tarjouspalvelu.fi -toimittajaportaalista.

title: On-site Document Shredding Services
description: This amendment is issued to address the following administrative and technical updates. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged: 1-Q&A: Posted the official Questions and Answers. 2-Period of Performance (POP): Corrected the POP dates. 3-Technical Exhibit 2.1: Corrected the exhibit by deleting the word "seventeen." 4-Clause Deletion: Removed clause 52.204-90. 5-Closing Date: Corrected the solicitation closing date. 6-Incumbent Information: Added the correct incumbent contractor's name and contract number. Please see attached Q@A for details This document is a Performance Work Statement (PWS) detailing the requirements for a non-personal services contract to provide mobile, on-site document shredding services for the Naval Education and Training Command (NETC) and the Naval Education and Training Professional Development Center (NETPDC) at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida. simple synopsis: Service: The contract is for on-site shredding of sensitive documents and materials containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII). Location: The services will be performed at three buildings on NAS Pensacola: Bldg. 603, Bldg. 3819, and Bldg. 628. Scope: The contractor must provide all personnel, equipment, and transportation. This includes supplying and servicing a total of forty-four 65-gallon containers and two 32-gallon consoles across the different locations, with service frequencies of every two or four weeks depending on the site. Key Requirements: The contractor is responsible for the secure collection, on-site destruction, and disposal of all paper materials. Destruction must comply with National Association of Information Destruction (NAID) standards and guidelines for Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). The contractor must also provide proof of destruction for each service visit. Personnel & Security: Contractor personnel must undergo background checks and obtain Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) credentials for base access. They must also adhere to strict conduct, safety, and security protocols. Period of Performance: The contract consists of a one-year base period (SEPT 1, 2026, to AUG 31, 2027) with four additional one-year option periods and -8 ( 6 MONTH EXT). Base Year: 01-SEP-2026 TO 31-AUG-2027 - Option Year 1: 01-SEP-2027 TO 31-AUG-2028 - Option Year 2: 01-SET-2028 TO 31-AUG-2029 - Option Year 3: 01-SEP-2029 TO 31-AGU-2030 - Option Year 4: 01-SEP-2030 TO 31-AUG-2031 - -8 Option Year 5: 01-SEP-2031 TO 1-MAR-2032

Submitted capability statements shall include sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to meet the requirement, including relevant experience, pricing information (if available), and supporting documentation. Submissions shall be sent via email to Contract Specialist, Emily H. Ryan at emily.h.ryan.civ@army.mil and Contracting Officer, Andrea M. Skilinski at andrea.m.skilinski.civ@army.mil. The anticipated award date is September 2026.

title: D--BAE GXP SOFTWARE MAINT
description: Intent to Award Notice - BAE GXP SOFTWARE MAINT The US Geological Survey (USGS) has a requirement to renew software maintenance for BAE Socet Set and Socet GXP for licenses residing USGS National Civil Applications Center (NCAC) classified facilities in Reston, VA and Lakewood, CO. The requirement is for continued maintenance support for the BAE Socet GXP geospatial software suite packaged for classified government work as the �Pro Bundle Upgrade Entitlement (UE).� The letters �UE� are included in the part number, and UE refers to upgrade entitlement software support. This means in addition to annual maintenance, new upgrades and releases are included as well. The software to be covered by this acquisition supports the national programs of the Core Science Systems (CSS) and National Land Imaging Program (NLI). The package is necessary to enhance the capacity for classified and unclassified stereo image processing in the NCAC Reston, VA and Lakewood, CO facilities. The total anticipated period of performance will be 10/01/2026 � 09/30/2027. The USGS is aware of no other source that can provide the above. Therefore, it intends to make an award to BAE unless it is contacted by any vendor who believes they have similar product that can meet the needs of this requirement. Vendors are invited to contact the Contract Specialist, Patrick Anderson via email at patrick_anderson@usgs.gov no later than 09:00 AM Eastern, Monday, August 24, 2026, with an affirmative answer.

title: RF Architectures Applying Photonic Timing and Routing (RAAPTR)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals to develop radiofrequency (RF) system architectures that employ and maintain optical timing precision in form factors and ruggedness traceable to compact mobile land, air, and space-based defense platforms. Proposals to the Radiofrequency (RF) Architectures Applying Photonic Timing and Routing (RAAPTR) program should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in vibration-hardened, ultra-low phase noise photonic oscillators; vibration-hardened, low phase noise ancillary analog and mixed-signal components; and high-performance analog and digital subsystem architectures that apply RAAPTR components to defense-relevant use cases and mission capabilities. Specifically excluded is research that advances non-optical methods of microwave generation or that results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. A Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) addendum provides additional details on the RAAPTR program. Please see Attachment A of this Program Solicitation (PS) for instructions on how to request the CUI Addendum. description: The Marine Corps Installations National Capital Region-Regional Contracting Office (MCINCR-RCO), on behalf of the Headquarters U.S. Marine Corps Human Resources and Organizational Management (HROM) Branch, is soliciting quotes for Leadership Training Seminar Services. The Contractor shall provide all labor, management, materials, student workbooks, licensed personality assessments, and fully burdened travel necessary to deliver seven (7) comprehensive, in-person training seminars (conducted at the Pentagon and MCB Quantico) over a 12-month Period of Performance. All training content must integrate modern adult-learning methodologies and address the specific core leadership competencies outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). This acquisition is being conducted under FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services), utilizing the simplified procedures authorized under FAR 12.203. This is an open-market, 100% total small business set-aside resulting in a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) purchase order awarded on a Best Value basis. The Government will evaluate quotations using a comparative assessment where non-price factors (Technical Capability and Past Performance), when combined, are significantly more important than price. The Government reserves the right to award to other than the lowest-priced quoter to secure a superior technical approach or reduced performance risk. Quotations must include a technical volume not exceeding five (5) pages (excluding sample material appendices) that details the proposed instructional approach, provides instructor biographies (no resumes), confirms the proposed standard personality assessment tool (e.g., DISC, Myers-Briggs), and explicitly confirms schedule compliance. Offerors must have an active SAM.gov registration (including complete Reps & Certs, UEI, and CAGE code) at the time of submission and hold pricing firm for 120 calendar days. All travel and incidental costs must be integrated directly into the proposed FFP unit price per seminar.

See CLINs in Attachment 3 � Price Schedule. (iii) Description of requirements: The Contractor shall provide comprehensive health insurance services in accordance with Attachment 1 � Statement of Work. Quoters are responsible for reviewing the entire solicitation package and all its following attachments: Attachment 1 � Statement of Work Attachment 2 � Employee and Salary Statistics Attachment 3 � Price Schedule Attachment 4 - Representations and Certifications Attachment 5 - IRS Form W-14 Attachment 6 - Instructions to Complete IRS Form W-14 Attachment 7 � Quick Registration Guide (SAM) The Contractor shall provide all health insurance services and benefits required under this contract for the firm-fixed unit prices specified herein. The unit prices shall include all costs associated with providing the required insurance coverage and administrative services, including labor, overhead, general and administrative expenses, profit, and, if applicable, Value-Added Tax (VAT), which shall be identified under a separate CLIN. Any costs not separately priced shall be considered included in the applicable unit prices as overhead, general and administrative expenses, or other indirect costs. No additional compensation shall be payable due to the Contractor's failure to properly estimate or accurately predict the costs or complexity of providing the required health insurance coverage and related administrative services. Except as otherwise expressly provided in the contract, the contract prices shall remain firm for the duration of the contract, and no adjustment shall be made based on increases in operating costs, labor costs, or fluctuations in currency exchange rates. The currency shall be fixed and cannot be changed by modification to the contract. VALUE ADDED TAX VAT is not applicable to this acquisition. Quoters shall not include VAT in CLIN prices unless otherwise specified in this solicitation. EXCISE TAX James Zadroga 9/11 Victims Health and Compensation Act of 2010 Notice: Unless a waiver or exception applies, payments subsequent to this procurement are subject to an excise tax of 2% pursuant to 26 U.S.C. 5000C. ECONOMIC PRICE ADJUSTMENT, PREMIUM ADJUSTMENT BASED ON EXPERIENCE Premium Adjustment Based on Experience - For health insurance, prices may be adjusted upward or downward based on the experience rating of the Mission(s) covered by this contract, and it specifically excludes all riders. No adjustment will be allowed during the base year. The Contractor or the Government may request an adjustment 60 days prior to the end of the base year or current option year, to take effect at the start of the following option year. Adjustments are not retroactive to previous periods of performance, and Contractors may not seek to recover costs incurred during a prior period of performance through an Economic Price Adjustment. Economic Price Adjustments only apply as an adjustment to the rates to be charged by the Contractor for the services identified as in the contract and cannot be recovered as a lump sum adjustment paid to the Contractor. Before any such adjustment is made, the Contractor agrees to provide the Government a balance sheet showing three main components for the time period: (1) receipts (premiums received) minus the retention amount; (2) number of insurance plans; and (3) claims paid. This information shall be provided per type of premium, i.e. per line item for the preceding 12 months. The retention amount is not subject to adjustment. The Government reserves the right to have an independent third party review the balance sheet and claims and make recommendations regarding the appropriateness of the requested adjustment. In that event, the Contracting Officer may enter into negotiations with the contractor to modify the contract to adjust the premium rate(s). The contractor agrees to provide all documentation necessary to support any requested adjustment. Employee Pool � This clause is only in effect if the contractor included details in its offer regarding a pooling arrangement, of which this contract is a part. Before any adjustment is made under this price adjustment clause, the contractor must include in its proposal for adjustment details setting forth how the pool impacts the request for equitable adjustment. title: Maintenance Agreement for NovaSeq 6000 sequencing system
description: NOTICE OF INTENT The National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Cancer Institute, intends to solicit and negotiate with Illumina, Inc. on a sole-source basis for preventive maintenance services for one (1) Government-owned Illumina NovaSeq 6000 sequencing system, Serial Number A01064. The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed-price contract for the required commercial services. The anticipated contract will be awarded pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The Government has determined that the required services are available from only one responsible source and that no other type of services will satisfy the Government's requirements. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The National Institutes of Health requires maintenance and preventive maintenance services for the following Government-owned equipment: Manufacturer: Illumina, Inc. Equipment: NovaSeq 6000 Serial Number: A01064 Quantity: One (1) The Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, technical expertise, materials, tools, equipment, and other resources necessary to maintain the equipment in proper operating condition. The required services are anticipated to include, but are not limited to: � Preventive maintenance in accordance with the manufacturer's recommended maintenance procedures; � Inspection, cleaning, testing, calibration, and adjustment of applicable system components; � Corrective maintenance and repair services; � Troubleshooting and diagnostic services; � Replacement of applicable failed or worn components; � Manufacturer-authorized replacement parts, as applicable; � Technical support; � Software and system configuration support associated with the NovaSeq 6000; � Performance verification following maintenance or repair; and � Documentation of maintenance and service activities. The Contractor shall perform maintenance services in accordance with applicable manufacturer specifications, technical requirements, and service procedures. SOLE-SOURCE BASIS The Government requires maintenance and technical support for an existing Illumina NovaSeq 6000 sequencing system, Serial Number A01064. The NovaSeq 6000 is a specialized sequencing platform manufactured by Illumina, Inc. The required maintenance and technical support are specific to the Government's existing system and require specialized technical knowledge and expertise associated with the equipment. The required services may include manufacturer-specific diagnostic procedures, proprietary software and configuration support, specialized service tools, manufacturer-authorized replacement parts, and technical procedures necessary to maintain and restore the system to proper operating condition. The Government's requirement is for continued maintenance of the existing NovaSeq 6000 rather than acquisition of a replacement sequencing system. Use of the existing equipment is necessary to support the Government's ongoing research activities and to minimize equipment downtime. Based on the Government's market research and knowledge of the equipment, Illumina, Inc. is the only responsible source reasonably believed to possess the necessary manufacturer-specific capability, technical expertise, service procedures, software/configuration support, and access to applicable manufacturer-authorized parts necessary to provide the required services for the Government's specific NovaSeq 6000, S/N A01064. Notice to Interested Parties This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, any responsible source, including small businesses, 8(a) firms, HUBZone small businesses, service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses (SDVOSBs), women-owned small businesses (WOSBs), veteran-owned small businesses (VOSBs), and small disadvantaged businesses (SDBs), may submit a capability statement demonstrating its ability to satisfy the Government's requirement. Capability statements will be evaluated solely to determine whether a competitive procurement should be conducted. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the Government's discretion. Anticipated Award The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of satisfying the Government's requirements. Capability statements must be submitted via email to haunp@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on August 24, 2026.

title: On-site Document Shredding Services
description: This document is a Performance Work Statement (PWS) detailing the requirements for a non-personal services contract to provide mobile, on-site document shredding services for the Naval Education and Training Command (NETC) and the Naval Education and Training Professional Development Center (NETPDC) at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida. simple synopsis: Service: The contract is for on-site shredding of sensitive documents and materials containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII). Location: The services will be performed at three buildings on NAS Pensacola: Bldg. 603, Bldg. 3819, and Bldg. 628. Scope: The contractor must provide all personnel, equipment, and transportation. This includes supplying and servicing a total of forty-four 65-gallon containers and two 32-gallon consoles across the different locations, with service frequencies of every two or four weeks depending on the site. Key Requirements: The contractor is responsible for the secure collection, on-site destruction, and disposal of all paper materials. Destruction must comply with National Association of Information Destruction (NAID) standards and guidelines for Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). The contractor must also provide proof of destruction for each service visit. Personnel & Security: Contractor personnel must undergo background checks and obtain Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) credentials for base access. They must also adhere to strict conduct, safety, and security protocols. Period of Performance: The contract consists of a one-year base period (SEPT 1, 2026, to AUG 31, 2027) with four additional one-year option periods and -8 ( 6 MONTH EXT). title: RF Architectures Applying Photonic Timing and Routing (RAAPTR)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals to develop radiofrequency (RF) system architectures that employ and maintain optical timing precision in form factors and ruggedness traceable to compact mobile land, air, and space-based defense platforms. Proposals to the Radiofrequency (RF) Architectures Applying Photonic Timing and Routing (RAAPTR) program should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in vibration-hardened, ultra-low phase noise photonic oscillators; vibration-hardened, low phase noise ancillary analog and mixed-signal components; and high-performance analog and digital subsystem architectures that apply RAAPTR components to defense-relevant use cases and mission capabilities. Specifically excluded is research that advances non-optical methods of microwave generation or that results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. A Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) addendum provides additional details on the RAAPTR program. Please see Attachment A of this Program Solicitation (PS) for instructions on how to request the CUI Addendum. The Proposer must request the CUI Addendum by the deadline stated in the Overview section.

title: Pre-Employment Screening Services - Federal Bureau of Prisons
description: The Bureau of Prisons (BOP) requires an immediate need for Comprehensive Medical Physical Examinations for Pre-Employment Screening Services. Applicants will schedule through a self-schedule or walk-in service. Examinations will include a medical assessment, mental health assessment, vision test, color vision test, hearing test, urinalysis, & fingerprinting. The contractor shall furnish all labor, equipment, supplies, facilities, and qualified medical personnel necessary to perform the services. The Bureau of Prisons has facilities throughout the nation: 118 institutions, 6 regional offices, a headquarters, 2 staff training centers, and 22 residential reentry management offices. The Federal Bureau of Prisons houses male and female offenders. All services will be performed at various locations and general information about BOP can be located at www.bop.gov. This posting is a "sources sought" notice. We are currently seeking information only from contractors capable of performing Pre-Employment Screening Services for all the identified areas of medical assessment, mental health assessment, vision test, color vision test, hearing test, urinalysis, & fingerprinting. Contractors are invited to respond to confirm interest in providing Comprehensive Medical Physical Examinations for Pre-Employment Screening Services. Please submit a brief response or capabilities statement. Emailed responses must be sent in .pdf format only to Nicasio Garcia, Contracting Officer at ngarcia@bop.gov. Include the following in your subject line: Sources Sought Response- Pre-Employment Screening Services. *Please note that responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This source sought is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or obligation on the part of the government. Neither unsolicited proposals nor any other kind of offers will be considered in response to this source sought. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement and/or any follow-up information requests. Interested parties may mark any response to be treated as business confidential information.

title: Ukraine – Security services – Security Guard Services for EUAM Ukraine
description: The proposed Framework Contract for the period 1 June 2027 to 31 May 2031 will ensure the continued provision of security guard services required to protect Mission personnel, facilities and assets, while enabling the uninterrupted implementation of the Mission's activities throughout the contract period in accordance with the EEAS Minimum Security Operating Standards and the EEAS Field Security Policy. The selected contractor will provide security guarding services for the EUAM HQ, Mission facilities and field presence on a 24/7 basis, including, but not limited to, the following services: a) Physical protection of Mission personnel, premises, equipment and other assets, including parking areas where applicable, as well as the accommodation of international Mission Members, in accordance with the highest applicable safety and security standards. b) Security services at Mission facilities, including access control during office hours, vehicle and visitor screening, internal and external patrols outside office hours, incident reporting, and monitoring of CCTV systems, intrusion alarms and fire detection systems. c) Security Response Teams (SRTs) responsible for monitoring designated patrol areas and responding to alarms or emergency calls at Mission offices and/or the accommodation of Mission Members.

title: Benchtop X-ray Diffractometer
description: CEI Mississauga Research Center is looking to acquire a Benchtop X-ray Diffractometer (XRD) to conduct analysis of material samples for Materials and Chemical Science applications. As such, the XRD must be capable of initially analyzing powder samples, small crystal samples, thin film samples, and metallic samples. Any equipment purchased must be able to be configured in future for work in the condition as requirements evolve. The Benchtop XRD must be easy to use and must have the requirements for re-alignment after reconfiguration of optical components reduced to a minimum – as such a ‘plug and play’ type system that can be implemented in automated workflows is required. The system requirements are listed below. All deliverables must be received no later than below: 20 weeks from the date of contract award.

title: Bio-capacitance probe system
description: Acquisition of a new four-probe system enabling real-time measurement of bio-capacitance for cell culture in bioreactors, for up to four bioreactors in parallel. This system will enable real-time estimation of viable cell concentration in those bioreactors. Measuring bio-capacitance at multiple frequencies, at regular intervals, in order to obtain the capacitance distribution spectrum of the cells, thereby enabling the real-time calculation of other critical cell culture parameters such as cell size, internal cell conductivity, and critical frequency. The probes to be acquired under this procurement must be compatible with the different types of bioreactors used by the team. In addition, the selected bio-capacitance probes must allow multi-frequency scanning for real-time determination of the intrinsic dielectric properties of the cells through analysis of the ß-dispersion of the signal using the Cole–Cole a model. Finally, the generated data must be capable of being captured in real time both by the control and data acquisition system via OPC-UA communication, and via 4–20 mA communication to enable integration of the probe directly into a control loop.

title: Multi-year Rental of an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV)
description: PART 1 – ADVANCE CONTRACT AWARD NOTICE (ACAN) An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. PART 2 – DEFINITION OF THE REQUIREMENT The Department of Natural Resources Canada (NRCan), through the Geological Survey of Canada – Atlantic, has a requirement to lease a proven deep-water autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) system on an annual basis, with options for renewal for up to five (5) years, to support seafloor mapping, marine geoscience, oceanographic research, Bedford Basin trials, Arctic collaborative research, and related Facility for Intelligent Marine Systems (FIMS) activities. The proposed requirement is for access to a HUGIN 1000 AUV system, or equivalent, including associated containerized support infrastructure, technical documentation, mission planning and support software, and remote technical support. The AUV system must provide reliable deep-water scientific survey capability and must be suitable for deployment from vessels of opportunity. The work will involve the following, as applicable: • Providing one (1) AUV system configured with a standard navigation and scientific sensor payload at lease commencement; • Providing one (1) climate-controlled 20-foot ISO container configured for storage, transport and maintenance of the AUV system; • Providing technical manuals, operational documentation, and mission planning/support software; • Providing basic remote technical assistance for normal operational use during the lease period; • Maintaining the AUV system in an operationally ready condition consistent with normal scientific survey use; • Maintaining insurance coverage for loss of or damage to the AUV system and associated containers for the duration of the lease period; and • Confirming system availability and readiness at the start of each lease year and notifying the Project Authority of issues that may affect system availability. PART 3 – CRITERIA FOR ASSESSMENT OF THE STATEMENT OF CAPABILITIES (MINIMUM ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS) Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: 3.1 Deep-water AUV capability: The Supplier must provide access to a proven autonomous underwater vehicle system rated to operate at a depth of at least 2,000 metres and suitable for scientific seafloor mapping and subsea data collection missions. 3.2 Navigation capability: The Supplier must provide an AUV system with an integrated navigation suite that includes inertial navigation, Doppler velocity log (DVL), and acoustic positioning capability, or equivalent navigation capability suitable for deep-water scientific survey operations. 3.3 Scientific survey sensor payload: The Supplier must provide an AUV system capable of supporting high-resolution seafloor mapping and subsea data collection using a multibeam echosounder, sidescan sonar, and sub-bottom profiler, or equivalent sensor capabilities that meet the scientific survey objectives. 3.4 Insurance for leased asset: The Supplier must confirm that insurance coverage for loss of or damage to the AUV system and associated containers will be maintained for the duration of the lease period. PART 4 – APPLICABILITY OF THE TRADE AGREEMENT(S) TO THE PROCUREMENT This procurement is subject to the following trade agreement(s): • Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) • Revised World Trade Organization - Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP) • Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) • Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) • Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA) • Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA) • Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA) • Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement (CUFTA) PART 5 – JUSTIFICATION FOR THE PRE-IDENTIFIED SUPPLIER The supplier mentioned in section 11 below is the only known supplier that meets the mandatory criteria set out in section 3 above. Should Canada receive a statement of capabilities from a supplier that contains sufficient information to indicate that it meets the requirements set forth in this ACAN, a competitive process will be triggered with a technical and financial evaluation methodology of the bids proposed by the potential bidders PART 6 – GOVERNMENT CONTRACTS REGULATIONS EXCEPTION(S) The following exception to soliciting bids under the Government Contracts Regulations is proposed, subject to approval and supporting documentation on file: • Subsection 6(d): only one person or firm is capable of performing the contract. The identified supplier, Université Laval, is the only one able to meet all of the criteria identified in paragraph 3 above. title: TBIPS - G.1. Geomatics Analyst – Level 2
description: The Department of National Defence requires three Geomatics Analysts – Level 2 to support the Mapping and Charting Establishment’s (MCE) Engineering Section. Under the direction of MCE Engineering staff, the Geomatics Analysts will contribute to the development and sustainment of geomatics engineering capabilities, IT infrastructure, and production workflows. The work to be conducted includes the creation, assessment, and manipulation of aeronautical and geospatial data; the development and evaluation of new datasets, applications, and production methods; the generation of digital aeronautical charts and specialized products that meet RCAF Operational Airworthiness (OA) requirements; and the provision of geomatics support to various Royal Canadian Air Force Project Management Offices (PMOs). This work will directly support capability development for programs such as CMLU and MHP.

title: Q301--MRI Phantom System Maintenance Intent to Sole Source
description: The Veteran s Administration (VA) Office of Research and Development, Regional Procurement Office East in Pittsburgh, PA intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Psychology Software Tools based in Sharpsburg, PA on behalf of the VA Salt Lake City Healthcare System. The requirement is to: Acquire 25 new Phantom systems manufactured by Psychology Software Tools, which may include storage and shipping when delivery is required. Engineering services to provide inspection, calibration, maintenance, Geometric Disk upgrades, and other upgrades to 105 currently installed Phantoms and up to 25 additional systems. The new Phantoms shall meet/exceed the specifications below and be 100% compatible with Phantom systems currently in-use at the VA facility. Website Development Services for the continuation of a project website already prototyped in collaboration with Psychology Software Tools. The systems will be used on an ongoing VA research study on Traumatic Brain Injuries (TBI). A Phantom is a precisely manufactured object of known size and composition that is imaged to test, adjust, or monitor; a Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) system s homogeneity, quantitative precision, and shape geometry for the purpose of quantification and correction of both measurement accuracy and quality. Phantoms attach to MRI scanners to collect and calibrate diagnostics for brain imaging. The VA research office currently uses phantoms supplied by Psychology Software Tools and must continue to use the same phantoms to maintain the integrity of research results. Too many variables from other systems can skew research data and some include proprietary magnets which are not compatible with the current system. The Phantom systems require calibration to the necessary proprietary format and require anisotropic diffusion, which is critical to diffusion imaging required by VA research. a. Acquisition of Geometric Distortion Disks for 100 Existing Phantom Devices. The minimum specifications are: Multiple geometric test points and patterns across a plane of the magnetic field Features support assessment of B1, B0 non-uniformity, geometric linearity, slice profile and slice positioning accuracy, resolution and SNR, etc. b. Additional MRI Calibration Phantoms Universal. The minimum specifications are: Phantom enclosure filled with deionized water with multiple internal test disks (1) Anisotropic Diffusion Disk 20+ anisotropic diffusion test points containing hollow micron scale (< 1 micron inside diameter) textile fibers Taxons to simulate diffusion characteristics of human axons for assessment of FA, AD, RD, MD. Variable packing densities 1.0, 0.5, 0.25/0.33, 0.125/0.67 Multiple tract sizes (1 6mm per side) Tract crossings of 90, 45, and 30 degrees (single tract size) (1) Isotropic Diffusion Disk includes 40+ NIST characterized fluids for assessment of T1,T2,T2*,PD,ADC (1) Spatial Homogeneity Disk includes Taxon fibers in X, Y, Z orientations to assess spatial homogeneity of diffusion (1) Pressure Compensation Disk & Thermometer maintains stable internal pressure during unit heating/cooling and shipping; internal thermometer (range of ~30-44°C) (1) Geometric Distortion Disk multiple geometric test points and patterns across a plane of the magnetic field features support assessment of B1, B0 non-uniformity, geometric linearity, slice profile and slice positioning accuracy, resolution and SNR, etc. Included Accessories: Heating and Storage Cabinet Head Coil Alignment Insert Insulated Hard Shell Rolling Shipping/Transport Case. c. Storage and Shipping Vendor to house up to 25 phantoms in secure, temperature-controlled environment and coordination of shipping and return shipping of phantom units to/from project scan sites (up to 4 one-way shipments per phantom). Storage for all 25 existing units during first period and then storage needs may be reduced based on need. Phantoms may be distributed to collaborating sites and will only cycle back to vendor in batches for inspection, assessment or upgrade/repair as needed. d. Engineering Services Evaluate custom phantom component options, testing of novel performance metrics, materials/component assessment, verification, reporting, etc., adaptation of head coil alignment inserts for use with new vendor head coil models. e. Engineering Services SEM / High Resolution Microscope assessment and reporting of all fiber LOTs included in each Phantom. f. Annual inspection service of existing phantom units Disassemble, inspect units for potential failures, reassemble, refill with deionized water, inspection report and comparison to baseline performance metrics. Any component repair/replacement that is not already covered under manufacturer s 1 year warranty shall be supported. The manufacturer is to provide discounted repair/replacement services relative to any standard terms for out-of-warranty repair services. g. Website development services - A project website is being prototyped for immediate deployment. The VA seeks additional web/software development services either directly or indirectly from the collaborators who designed and developed the first phase of the web-based software system. The estimated requirement is up to 240 hours of development services over a 12-month period). ADDITIONAL SERVICES ON NEWLY ACQUIRED DEVICES Service, Recondition, MRI Calibration Phantom: Return of unit service aft er 1 year of use for evaluation, reconditioning/recalibration, and component upgrades. Includes free upgrade of any internal components to any improved models/revisions. Storage & Shipping: Secure temperature-controlled storage of inventory units for up to one year with multiple shipments to test sites as directed. The requirement will take place at a VA facility in Salt Lake City, UT. The sole source is pursuant to FAR 6.302-1 Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, however; any responsible source who believes it is capable of meeting the requirement may submit a capability statement and supporting documentation to the contracting office no later than Monday, August 24, 2026 (10:00 AM, EST). Interest/capability statements may be sent to Michael Haydo at Michael.haydo@va.gov. No telephone responses will be accepted. A determination not to compete the proposed requirement based upon the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: Notice of Intent for NIH/NIA GraphPad Prism Subscription Renewal
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT, NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. A REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) WILL NOT BE ISSUED AND QUOTES WILL NOT BE REQUESTED. The National Institute of Health National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to award a firm fixed price sole source contract under the authority of FAR 12.102(a), only one source being available to meet the Government's needs, to: GraphPad Software, LLC 225 Franklin St FL 26 Boston, MA, 02110 The NIA hereby submits a notice of intent to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order for Prism Group Academic Yearly Subscription with 300 activations for their Intramural Research Program (IRP). The Computational Biology and Genomics Core (CBGC) requires a comprehensive, powerful, and user-friendly statistical and graphing software license subscription for the National Institute on Aging (NIA) Intramural Research Program (IRP). Most NIA-IRP research scientists need intuitive statistical and graphing software that integrates seamlessly with Microsoft Excel. Prism offers a familiar, Excel-like interface and is specifically designed for the types of analyses experimental scientists perform. GraphPad Prism tracks and organizes a scientist�s work in a unique way, linking data, graphs, and analyses together. Changes in data automatically update all related analyses and graphs. Prism includes help and teaching information to guide a scientist in choosing a statistical test and creating the appropriate graph. Purchasing an institute-wide license will benefit the majority of experimental scientists at NIA-IRP and be more cost-effective than acquiring individual licenses. NIA-IRP has been using this software since 2006 or earlier. Over the past 5-6 years, CBGC has acquired varying numbers of seats, and there is now a need to purchase 300 seats to meet current demand. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541519. The period of performance will be for one (1) 12-month base period from date of award to August 14. 2027. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for the requirement. This hereby constitutes a synopsis of the requirement. CLOSING STATEMENT The determination not to compete this proposed contract action is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice. This is NOT a request for quotes or proposals. Questions or comments to this Notice of Intent should be directed to the Primary Point of Contact Leah L. Hinson via e-mail only Leah.Hinson@hhs.gov (no phone calls/voice mail). Messages regarding questions will not be accepted and will not receive a response). Please indicate in the subject of your email: Notice of Intent Question Submission � PCA-NIA�06255 GraphPad Prism Subscription Renewal. (Acceptance will be determined by the customer � DoWEA.) AVC�s project scope of work shall include providing and installing all needed new infrastructure, or modifications to existing infrastructure, to produce the new Audio Visual systems. The AVC�s scope shall also include all engineering and design services necessary to determine the details and extent of any needed infrastructure. Infrastructure includes, but not limited to: i. Electrical Power and Distribution (EC license may be required) ii. Rigging and Hanging Hardware, Including Pipes, Grids, Suspensions, Fastening, Reinforcement, and Fly-ware iii. description: Request for Information / Sources Sought Notice for Providers/Suppliers of Mecademic Robotics MECA500-R4-OB Robot Arm (BRAND NAME OR EQUAL) Notice ID: NIST-AMD-SSN-26-02447 Contract Opportunity Type Sources Sought Response Date: August 24, 2026 @ 10:00 AM, ET Product Service Code 3693 - Industrial Assembly Machines NAICS Code 333998 - All Other Miscellaneous General Purpose Machinery Manufacturing with the small business size standard of 700 employees. BACKGROUND This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) for industry to help the Government determine the availability and capability of small business and other than small businesses which can provide any or all of the products and services required by the U.S. Department of Commerce, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). NIST is conducting market research to identify potential sources that can provide a Mecademic Robotics MECA500-R4-OB Robot Arm (OR EQUAL) that meets all technical specifications identified in this notice. This notice is strictly to request information for market research purposes to help NIST determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for this requirement. This notice shall not be construed as a solicitation, an obligation, or commitment by NIST. OVERVIEW The Intelligent Systems Division (ISD) of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) needs a Mecademic Robotics MECA500-R4-OB (or equivalent) ROBOT ARM suitable for robotic assembly applications and portable for demonstrations. One of the programmatic goals of this effort is to demonstrate and develop tests for different robotic manufacturing applications. NIST requires one (1) Mecademic Robotics MECA500-R4-OB (or equivalent) ROBOT ARM, including hardware, software, accessories, calibration certificate, and warranty. The delivered system shall include everything necessary for immediate operation in a laboratory environment. LINE ITEM 1: Quantity One (1) each, Mecademic Robotics MECA500-R4-OB (Brand Name or Equivalent) ROBOT ARM The ROBOT ARM must meet the following minimum salient characteristics: The ROBOT ARM must have a minimum payload that meets or exceeds 0.5 kg. The ROBOT ARM must have a minimum arm reach of 330 mm (or more). The ROBOT ARM must weigh less than or equal to 5 kg without any cables. The ROBOT ARM must have a position repeatability of less than or equal to � 0.005 mm. The ROBOT ARM must have Six (6) degrees of freedom. The ROBOT ARM must have black surface finish to absorb 90% visible light or higher. LINE ITEM 2: Quantity One (1) each, PS200-R4 POWER SUPPLY (OR EQUAL) The POWER SUPPLY must be compatible with the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1 and have appropriate connectors that fit the ROBOT ARM. LINE ITEM 3: Quantity One (1) each, MGC-HFA COMMUNICATION CABLE (OR EQUAL) The COMMUNICATION CABLE must be compatible with LINE ITEM 1 and the GRIPPERS in LINE ITEM 5 and LINE ITEM 6 LINE ITEM 4: Quantity One (1) each, MUAP01 universal ADAPTER PLATE (OR EQUAL) The ADAPTER PLATE must meet the following minimum salient characteristics: The ADAPTER PLATE must be of the size 125 mm � 100 mm for mounting the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1 on an aluminum T-slotted profile and optical breadboards of 25 mm pitch. LINE ITEM 5: Quantity One (1) each, MEGP-25E electric GRIPPER (OR EQUAL) The GRIPPER must have the following minimum salient characteristics: The GRIPPER must be compatible with the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1. The GRIPPER must have a stroke of 6 mm (or more). The GRIPPER must be able to grip with a force of 40 N (or more). A power/energy source for the GRIPPER must be provided. The power/energy for the GRIPPER may be provided through the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1. LINE ITEM 6: Quantity One (1) each, MEGP-25LS electric GRIPPER (OR EQUAL) The GRIPPER must have the following minimum salient characteristics: The GRIPPER must be compatible with the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1 The GRIPPER must have a stroke of 48 mm (or more). The GRIPPER must be able to grip with a force of 40 N (or more). A power/energy source for GRIPPER must be provided. The power/energy for the GRIPPER may be provided through the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1. LINE ITEM 7: Quantity One (1) each, MPM500 PNEUMATIC MODULE (OR EQUAL) The PNEUMATIC MODULE must be compatible with the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1 and provides an interface with various pneumatic tools. LINE ITEM 8 : Quantity One (1) each, Mecademic MECA DEMO CASE (OR EQUAL) The DEMO CASE must be a waterproof & shockproof hard case with wheels and an adjustable handle that can carry the ROBOT ARM in LINE ITEM 1 WARRANTY The contractor shall warrant the entire system for a minimum of one year after acceptance. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial construction prepared in accordance with the format in RFO subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This requirement is for the delivery and installation of security cameras at Whiteman AFB, MO. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, tools, transportation, vehicles, and equipment necessary to install wired infrastructure cameras on the exterior of bldgs. 2001, 2005, pump station to the west of 2005, light pole east side 5032, 5034, 5035 (interior), 5036, 5048, 50010, and headworks station at waste-water plant. A total of 13 cameras will be installed, 11 cameras shall have the PTZ (pan-tilt-zoom) capability to be repositioned remotely from each of the monitoring sites, 2 cameras installed inside 5035 and headworks station are static cameras. Please see full solicitation details at attachments.

description: Enclosed is the Request for Quotations (RFQ) for Sport Utility Vehicle (SUV). If you would like to submit a quotation, follow the instructions at the bottom of the RFQ document. title: 78--2026 Steel Pavilions
description: Amendment 0007: The purpose of this amendment is to provide answers to submitted questions: 1. Snow and Wind Design Criteria: The specifications state that the structures must meet site-specific snow and wind load criteria, while the actual ground snow load and wind speed values are left �to be determined by site specific design.� Please confirm whether the contractor/manufacturer is responsible for determining these site-specific design loads through its licensed engineer, or whether BLM will provide the required design values. A1. This amendment hereby modifies requirements 4 & 5 of the attached specification to remove CUSTOM wind and snow load requirements. Wind and snow load requirements shall be based on building codes applicable to the delivery locations. 2. Delivery Schedule: The solicitation establishes a delivery date of October 30, 2026. Please confirm whether all required shelters must be delivered and accepted by this date and whether partial or phased deliveries are permitted. A2. The delivery due date for all items is 01/31/2027 3. Scope of Work: Please confirm that the contractor�s scope is limited to furnishing, transporting, and offloading the Rob Jaggers Campground shelters, including the required engineered drawings, foundation/footing design, and installation instructions. The specifications require the manufacturer to provide engineered drawings and foundation/footing design, and state that the contractor is responsible for offloading. Please confirm that field erection, concrete foundations/footings, anchoring, and final installation are not included in the contractor�s scope. A3. This is correct... Supply delivery and tech data only Amendment 0006: In response to a vendor submitted question: Q1. The summary and coating paragraph indicate 24 shelters, while the post/upright color paragraph indicates 27. Page 1 also includes a �Quantity: 8 Total� reference. Could you please confirm the total number of shelters we should use for pricing purposes? A1. The requirement is for the following quantities. Any inconsistencies to volume shall be clarified to the following. CLIN 00011: 10 ft x 10 ft prefabricated Steel Pavilion, 24 each, Rob Jaggers Campground (incl freight) CLIN 00020: 20 FT X 20 FT prefabricated Steel Pavilion, 1 each, Datil Campground CLIN 00030: 16 FT X 16 FT prefabricates Steel Pavilion, 4 each, Datil Campground CLIN 00040: Freight costs allocable to Datil Campground Amendment 0005: The purpose of this modification is to clarify prior question and answer. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. 3. Post/Upright Quantity: Under the coating requirements, the specifications reference color selection for the "24 each � 10' x 10'" post/uprights, while the procurement is for 24 shelters. Please confirm that this is a typographical error and that the requirement applies to all posts/uprights associated with the 24 shelters. RE: Datil Well CG Shelters ONLY � Minimum Specifications: Quantity of 5 (five) as specified: 1. Length x Width -20 feet x 20 feet to roofline (1 each): all steel, square, hip roof shelters 2. Length x Width - 16 feet x 16 feet to roofline (4 each): all steel, square, hip roof shelters RFO: Rob Jaggers Faciltiy requires quantity of 24 Each. Total = 24 � 10� x 10� (RFO NCA) + 5 (SFO Datil CG) = 29 total to 2 different locations Amendment 0004: The purpose of this modification is to provide the below questions and answers. 1. Snow and Wind Loads: The specifications state that the ground snow load and wind speed loading are to be determined by site-specific design(by manufacturer), but the required PSF and MPH values are blank. Can BLM provide the required ground snow load and design wind speed for the Rob Jaggers Campground location? RE: Datil Well CG Shelters ONLY � these values are blank as a requirement of the building manufacturer to calculate and provide in the response to this solicitation. title: 66--Special Notice of Intent to Sole Source Award
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Award THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Communications Branch intends to award a firm fixed price sole source under the authority of FAR subpart 13.106-1(b)(1)(i) and (ii), for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), Contracting Officers may solicit from only one source if the circumstances deem only one source is reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand name, or industrial mobilization).: YSI, INC. 1725 Brannum LN Yellow Springs, Ohio 45387-1107, United States The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334516, Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing, and the Product Service Code (PSC) for this requirement is 6640, Laboratory Equipment and Supplies. The object of this sole source award is to require the purchase of SonTek RS5 Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler (ADCP) to enable accurate and defensible measurement of streamflow in a wide range of field conditions. This device supports the direct collection of discharge data in both shallow and deep channels, including high velocity environments, and includes integrated quality assurance features that allow staff to review and document measurements in the field for regulatory and water rights purposes. The system must be fully portable, self contained, and field ready, as staff have limited time for equipment assembly or configuration prior to deployment and routinely conduct measurements at multiple sites in a single day. The device must also be compatible with the current program inventory of existing hydroboards, GNSS equipment, and established hydrologic workflows which are required to produce output files that can be incorporated into the WISKI database without custom programming. Accurate and repeatable streamflow measurements are required for National Wildlife Refuge (NWR) and National Fish Hatchery (NFH) water rights protection, ecological water management, and compliance with state mandated monitoring requirements. Without this equipment, WRB risks delays or inaccuracies in required flow measurements, which could lead to violations of state water rights conditions at significant cost to the government. The SonTek RS5 is the only ADCP that meets WRB operational and integration needs because it offers integrated RTK/GNSS, confirmed GPS compatibility, broad depth suitability, lightweight deployment, and a fully self contained design with built in power and communications. All other vendors researched, were determined to not be suitable for meeting WRB needs. This synopsis does not constitute a solicitation; however, if any interested party believes they can meet the above requirement, it may submit a statement of capabilities. The statement of capabilities must be submitted in writing and must contain clear and convincing evidence that competition of this requirement would be advantageous to the Government. If parties choose to respond, any cost associated with preparation and submission of data or any other cost incurred in response to this announcement are the sole responsibility of the respondent and will not be reimbursed by the Government. Capability statements shall be submitted by e-mail ONLY as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to the following address: carter_duke@ios.doi.gov. NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS/OFFERS WILL BE HONORED

title: 6350--Demountable Wall System
description: Statement of Work (SOW) Headache Center of Excellence Demountable Walls, Adaptive Lighting, and Sound System James A. Haley Veterans Hospital (JAHVH) 13000 Bruce B. Downs Blvd Tampa, FL 33612 1.0 Background The James A. Haley Veterans Hospital (JAHVH) requires installation of a demountable wall system integrated with adaptive lighting and sound control technology to support clinical operations within the Headache Center of Excellence (HCoE). The HCoE provides care to Veterans experiencing chronic headaches, polytrauma, and traumatic brain injury conditions that cause heightened sensitivity to bright lighting, noise, and visual stimuli. Current clinic spaces rely on fixed, bright lighting that can exacerbate pain and limit Veterans ability to participate in clinical assessments and therapies. A controlled sensory environment is essential for reducing symptom triggers and improving clinical outcomes. The Vendor shall manage all ordering, shipment, installation, configuration, and debris removal related to the demountable wall system, adaptive lighting and sound equipment, and any associated furniture. 2.0 Purpose The purpose of this project is to install a demountable wall system equipped with healthcare appropriate adaptive lighting and sound control features. The upgraded system will allow clinicians to adjust environmental conditions to meet individual Veteran sensitivity levels, reducing light or noise induced discomfort and supporting therapies such as biofeedback, relaxation, and TBI related headache management. This project enhances patient comfort, improves safety, and aligns the HCoE environment with modern therapeutic standards for patients requiring specialized sensory control. 3.0 Statement of Work The Vendor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, installation, programming, and configuration required to deliver a complete demountable wall system with integrated adaptive lighting and sound components. All products shall meet VA clinical environment standards for cleanability, durability, and infrastructure compatibility.

title: SITE VISIT - MRI System Installation - NIH Bldg. 10 Laboratory
description: SOLICITATION TYPE: Pre-Solicitation / Mandatory Site Visit Announcement PROJECT TITLE: High-Power 7T MRI System Installation & Rigging � NIH Building 10 PSC CODE: N065 (Installation of Equipment- Medical, Dental, and Veterinary) NAICS CODE: 334510 (Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing) 1. MANDATORY SITE VISIT CLAUSE (FAR 52.237-1): A physical site visit is strictly mandatory. Due to the extreme weight, multi-ton structural load, stray magnetic fields, and complex rigging paths required to install a 7-Tesla (7T) magnet inside an active clinical hospital, visual blueprints and photographs are insufficient for proposal formulation. 2. LOGISTICS (DATE, TIME, & LOCATION): - DATE: September 3, 2026 - TIME: 10:00 AM EDT - LOCATION: NIH Bethesda Campus, Building 10 (Assembly point: B1 NMR Loading Dock) 3. PRE-REGISTRATION / ACCESS AND SECURITY PROTOCOLS DEADLINE: Building 10 is a secure clinical research facility. All attendees must pre-register by emailing the Point of Contact (POC) listed below no later than August 24, 2026, at 10:00 AM EDT with their Full Legal Name and Company Name. Unregistered individuals will be denied entry to the campus and the facility. A maximum of two (2) representatives per firm is permitted. Attendees must bring a valid government-issued photo ID to clear campus perimeter security gates and must remain with their NIH escort at all times. PRE-REGISTRATION SUBMISSION FORM: Prospective bidders must copy, complete, and paste the following form into the body of their RSVP email to the Point of Contact (POC). Do not alter the format. ==================================================================== NIH BUILDING 10 SITE VISIT PRE-REGISTRATION SUBMISSION ==================================================================== 1. Company Legal Name: _____________________________________________ 2. Company UEI (Unique Entity ID): _________________________________ 3. Attendee 1 Full Legal Name (As shown on ID): ____________________ 4. Attendee 1 Citizenship (US Citizen / Permanent Resident / Foreign National): ______________ 5. Attendee 2 Full Legal Name (As shown on ID): ____________________ 6. Attendee 2 Citizenship (US Citizen / Permanent Resident / Foreign National): ______________ 7. Primary Phone Number for Day of Event: _________________________ ==================================================================== 4. DISQUALIFICATION WARNING: Bids submitted by vendors who fail to pre-register by the deadline, or who fail to physically attend and sign the official attendance log at the site visit, will be deemed non-responsive and automatically disqualified from award consideration. 5. OBJECTIVE: The specific objective of this purchase is the acquisition of a 7T MRI System with a dedicated, high-performance, local gradient subsystem. The acquisition will allow the Functional MRI Facility (FMRIF) to be able to provide the latest tools and techniques to NIH researchers to collect high quality brain imaging data from patients and research volunteers and develop novel scanning protocols advancing the state-of-the-art for structural and functional brain imaging. The upgraded system is to be used for clinical and preclinical human MRI research. The baseline requirement is for the immediate delivery and installation of the 7T MRI system. However, bidders must note that the requesting lab intends to include certain optional items listed below as (OPTION) as executable options for the following fiscal year. Bidders should evaluate the site during the walkthrough with future system scaling in mind." Baseline Product : 1. Baseline Brand Name Model: Siemens MAGNETOM Terra.X with Impulse Local Gradient Coil - Qty (1) EA 2 . Turn-Key Contruction & Installation - Qty (1) 3. Multinuclear Support and Applications (OPTION ) - Qty (1) EA 4. Terra to Terra.X upgrade: Software upgrade - Qty (2) EA 5. Terra to Terra.X ugrade: FDA-cleared 8Tx32Rx Head Coil Exchange - (OPTION) Qty (2) EA 6. Terra to Terra.X upgrade: Gradient Performance - Qty (2) EA 6. COMPETITION AND PROPRIETARY DATA NOTICE: This is an open, competitive solicitation utilizing a Brand Name or Equal description. To ensure a fair and transparent bidding environment, no proprietary manufacturer floor plans, engineering layouts, or equipment diagrams are attached to this notice. Bidders are expected to engineer their technical proposals based on the physical parameters gathered during the mandatory site inspection. 7. SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS (BRAND NAME OR EQUAL): The procurement utilizes the Siemens Healthineers MAGNETOM Terra.X 7T MRI platform as the baseline standard. Any alternative system proposed must meet or exceed the following minimal physical and structural characteristics to fit existing infrastructure: - Field Strength: Active-shielded 7.0-Tesla (7T) superconducting magnet. - Operational Weight: Total operational weight must align with Building 10 B1 structural floor load-bearing limits for heavy medical infrastructure. - Stray Field Footprint: The 5-Gauss safety boundary line must fit completely within the designated laboratory room envelope without penetrating adjacent active clinical or public corridors. - Cryogen Venting: System must be compatible with existing facility structural routing paths for high-volume helium cryogen quench pipe exhaust loops. SEE ATTACHMENT. 8. INSTRUCTIONS FOR SUBMITTING POST-VISIT WRITTEN QUESTIONS: To ensure all prospective bidders receive identical information, the NIH will not provide verbal answers to technical questions during the physical site visit. All inquiries must be handled through the formal written process detailed below: 1. SUBMISSION DEADLINE: All technical, structural, or contractual questions resulting from the site visit must be submitted via email no later than September 8, 2026, before/prior to 11:00 AM EDT. 2. SUBMISSION METHOD: Questions must be sent directly to the POC email listed below. The email subject line must strictly read: "TECHNICAL QUESTIONS: NIH Bldg. 10 MRI Installation - [Insert Vendor Name]". 3. METHOD OF RESPONSE: The NIH will aggregate all vendor questions, remove identifying company names, and publish the official answers collectively. This will be posted as a formal Amendment to this solicitation on SAM.gov on or about September 10, 2026. Only written answers published via SAM.gov shall be considered legally binding. 9. POINT OF CONTACT: Submit pre-registration data and written technical inquiries to: Tina Robinson @ robinsti@mail.nih.gov. 10. CONTRACTOR RESPONSIBILITY FOR DATA COLLECTION: Bidders are explicitly notified that the Government will not provide physical facility dimensions, structural tolerances, or site architectural drawings under this open solicitation. It is the sole responsibility of the attending vendor representatives to physically take all necessary measurements, calculations, photographs, and environmental assessments during the walkthrough. Bidders must bring their own measuring tools (laser measures, tape measures) and equipment. Photographs are permitted within the target laboratory space for structural, electrical, and plumbing engineering purposes only. No photography of hospital personnel, clinical patient care areas, or public corridors is permitted. Failure to accurately measure the site layout will not relieve the successful contractor from the responsibility of successfully executing the system installation at no additional cost to the Government

title: Telemetry System-9390P08
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention intends to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order to Infrared Telemetrics Inc. 1780 Birch St., MI 49930-1072 (CAGE Code: 3M7H3) for the purchase of a Telemetry System-9390P08 for development of seismic potential forecasting methods. Description This contract action is for the purchase of a Telemetry System-9390P08 for Development of Seismic Potential Forecasting Methods. The contractor shall provide a radio frequency telemetry system capable of collecting sensor data from roof bolting machines during operation. The system shall include all required components, accessories, and documentation needed for operation. The objective is to collect data from the rotating drill steel of a roof bolting machine, where traditional wiring is not practical. The system must be capable of operating in high vibration environments, such as internal combustion engines, automotive transmissions, and rotating machinery, and must be demonstrated to maintain reliable data collection under these conditions. The system must also include universal signal conditioning to support strain gauges, load cells, accelerometers, and other compatible sensors. The system shall be capable of operating in high vibration environments and shall include signal conditioning to support strain gauges and accelerometers. The data collected will support efforts to identify structurally unsound roof conditions and improve mine safety. The contractor shall provide the following components: � One single channel analog radio frequency transmitter for acceleration � One single channel analog radio frequency transmitter for strain � One inductive power converter with pick up coil � One Model 1051 inductive power supply � One custom inductive exciter coil with mounting hardware and integral receiving antennas The contractor shall provide design, machining, and assembly of a clamp-on transmitter housing containing the transmitters and power converter. The housing shall be designed to mount directly to the drill steel. The system shall be delivered in fully functional condition. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 12.102 and 12.201-1. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, all quotations responses received by Monday, 24 August 2026 at 10:00 am Eastern Standard Time (EST) of the issuance of this notice will be considered by the government. A determination by the government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Any quotations /responses should be emailed to Sandra Adams at ab41@cdc.gov by Monday, 24 August 2026.

Prices must be all-inclusive and must cover all costs associated with providing the services, including but not limited to labor, materials, equipment, supervision, transportation, and any other costs. description: The 22d Contracting Squadron (22 CONS) at McConnell AFB, Kansas, intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract for the procurement, delivery, installation, and integration of a modernized Audio/Visual (AV) system for the Bleckley Lounge, located within the Dole Community Center. The Bleckley Lounge is a multi-purpose venue utilized for official training, retirements, promotion ceremonies, events, and meetings. The objective of this requirement is to execute a targeted AV system refresh that improves video display capabilities, AV source routing, and centralized control while seamlessly integrating with existing Government-retained equipment (e.g., amplification, loudspeakers, wireless microphones). Additionally, this solicitation includes one (1) Optional line item (Option 1) to provide the necessary equipment, programming, and labor to integrate the refreshed Bleckley Lounge AV system with the adjacent Tavern AV system, enabling bidirectional audio/video routing and unified control between the two spaces. title: Intent to Sole Source: Absolute RSD - Office Space Renovation
description: Amendment 001 is to extend the response date from 08/21/2026 to 08/24/2026 and provide responses to questions concerning this solicitation. Please see attached. *********************************************************************************************** The Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB) requires renovation and buildout services for leased office space located on the 5th Floor of TTB Headquarters at 1310 G Street NW, Washington, DC 20005. The requirement is for a complete office renovation to reconfigure existing leased space in support of TTB mission operations. The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, permits (as required), and incidentals necessary to perform the renovation in accordance with Government-furnished concept drawings and the Statement of Work. The work includes, but is not limited to: Selective demolition. Reuse and relocation of existing doors. Construction of new non-structural perimeter and office partitions. Installation and finishing of gypsum board to a Level 4 finish. Limited ceiling removal, reinstallation, and replacement. Removal and replacement of carpet and cove base. Painting of renovated areas. Relocation of sprinkler heads. Installation of HVAC transfer ducts and relocation of ductwork and registers. Electrical and fire alarm modifications, including demolition of affected outlets and lighting; recircuiting lighting at new demising walls; installation of thirty-six (36) 2x4 LED light fixtures; installation of five (5) edge-lit exit lights; installation of nine (9) single-pole switches; installation of forty-eight (48) duplex receptacles served by eight (8) 20-amp/120-volt circuits; installation of twelve (12) ring-and-string pathways; installation of two (2) two-circuit furniture feeds; and relocation of five (5) existing fire alarm strobes. Final cleaning and delivery of the renovated space in a condition ready for Government occupancy. Subject to final approval, Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC, formerly Fiscal Service Procurement) on behalf of the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB) intends to make award on a sole source basis in accordance with FAR 6.302-1, to Absolute RSD, LLC, for the renovation of existing spaces in TTB headquarters located at 1310 G St NW, Washington, DC. The Lessor will only permit their approved contractors into the building to perform these services. Absolute RSD, LLC is the authorized contractor to perform work in this facility. TTB will consider written responses received no later than 11:00 am ET on August 21, 2026. Responses must include sufficient evidence that clearly shows the vendor can provide the renovation of spaces. If no written response is received that clearly demonstrates an ability to meet these requirements, is more advantageous to the Government, and is received by the deadline, TTB, shall make award on a sole source basis to Absolute RSD, LLC.
